title: Merging adjacent rules with *almost* the same declarations
impact: 12 thumbs-up, the most-requested of these three. Reporter's case is Framer-generated site CSS; a 2024 comment names it as the main size gap vs csso. Real corpus, adjacent pairs with a profitable safe factoring (raw bytes): Bootstrap 39 pairs / 2,919 B (1.27%), Radix Themes 91 / 4,474 B (0.66%), Bulma 7 / 4,071 B (0.60%), Primer 0.04%, Font Awesome / Pico <0.1%, react-spectrum S2 / animate / open-props 0. Custom-property-only factoring accounts for 1,801 B of Bootstrap, 4,049 B of Bulma and 2,022 B of Radix.
summary: Adjacent rules that share some declarations are not factored (`.foo{bg:red;padding:20px}.bar{bg:red;padding:40px}` stays as is). Factoring to `A,B{common}A{rest}B{rest}` is safe for adjacent rules only if no shared declaration overlaps a non-shared one in either rule (same property, shorthand/longhand, logical/physical like `width`/`inline-size`, `all`), importance is kept separate, neither rule has nested rules, and the combined selector list passes `is_compatible`. It only pays off when the shared text exceeds the extra selector text (maintainer's comment), and the gain is mostly in raw rather than compressed size.

draftReply:
Status update: this still doesn't happen on the latest release. For adjacent rules it can be done safely, but only when no shared declaration overlaps another declaration in either rule. That covers the same property, a shorthand and its longhands, logical and physical pairs like `width`/`inline-size`, and `all`. The selectors also have to be safe to combine into one list. As noted above, it only helps when the shared declarations are longer than the extra selectors.

On real stylesheets the raw saving is about 0.6-1.3% for Bootstrap, Bulma and Radix Themes, and close to zero for others. Much of it comes from repeated custom properties, and there's an open draft PR, #1333, that factors those out. After gzip/brotli the gain is a lot smaller.
